title: About
text:
I build models that support basketball decisions: when an injured player will be back, what a shot or a rebound chance is really worth, and how much the schedule tilts the standings.
I came to basketball analytics from quantitative trading, where I spent three years at two firms building statistical models that had to hold up when real money was on the line. That background shapes how I work: calibrated probabilities, honest validation against a benchmark, and outputs a decision-maker can act on without asking me how to read them.

title: About
text:
Experience
Oklahoma City Thunder: Data Science Intern (Summer 2026)

Built a Bayesian hierarchical survival model forecasting player return-to-play dates, scoring a 0.53 Brier skill score against Rotowire’s published timelines on held-out injuries
Built the ETL pipeline behind it: an episode-level dataset of roughly 8,000 injuries across five seasons
Delivered forecasts, injury histories and comparable-injury cohorts to front office and performance staff through a Streamlit app

Geneva Trading: Quantitative Metals Trader (2023–2024)
Quantitative strategies across futures and options, including a relative-value model trading precious metals against interest-rate products.
XR Trading: Quantitative Crypto Trader (2021–2022)
Low-latency multi-exchange arbitrage systems, post-trade analytics, and research on market microstructure and lead-lag dynamics.

title: About

Education
The University of Chicago: M.S., Applied Data Science
Capstone: a physics-informed variational autoencoder for prostate MRI that roughly tripled the accuracy of tissue measurements over the clinical baseline, with uncertainty intervals calibrated to hold on 7 of 9 parameters.
The University of Texas at Austin: B.S. Computer Science (Turing Scholars Honors), B.B.A. (Business Honors), B.S. Mathematics

title: Basketball analytics for front-office decisions
text:
I’m Aaron Garay, a data scientist, former quant trader, and former Data Analyst Intern with the Oklahoma City Thunder. This site collects side projects that each answer a question a front office actually asks: who’s at risk of injury, which shots and rebounds a team should be getting, how hard a schedule really is, and how teams value assets in trades.
Every project is built from public data, with code linked and validation shown.
